sections.heading: 1. Easier on the wrists
lines: ① Drop to forearms, or lean on a soft fist.
② Press through finger bases and thumb pad.
③ Pop a folded towel under the heel of the hand.
④ Hands and knees, 10 sec × 5; build over weeks.

slides.title:
Meet Hybi at Hybrid Physio!

caption:
Momo loves Pilates, but her wrists grumble every time class goes into a plank. Planks and hands and knees work load the wrist while it's bent right back, which is a big ask if your wrists aren't used to it.

The good news: Pilates is easy to adapt. Try forearms or a soft fist instead of a flat hand, press through your finger bases and thumb pad, and pop a folded towel under the heel of your hand. Build tolerance with short holds over a few weeks. Most importantly, tell your instructor at the start of class.

Swelling or tingling fingers are worth getting checked. Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physio tailors sessions to you. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
